mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, Exalted is He, {وَهُوَ الله فِي السَّمَاوَات وَفِي الأَرْض يعلم}: if you make وَفِي الأَرْض attached (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it, you pause at وَفِي الأَرْض and put يعلم in the nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), its implied form being "He is the One worshipped in the heavens and on the earth". And if you make وَفِي الأَرْض attached to يعلم, you pause at السَّمَوَات.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {ألم يرَوا كم أهلكنا}: كم is in the position of the accusative governed by أهلكنا, not by يروا, because what precedes an interrogative, or what takes its course and resembles it, does not govern it.
His saying {مدرارا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السَّمَاء.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {مَا كَانُوا بِهِ}: it is in the position of the nominative as the agent of حاق, and its implied form is "the punishment of what they used to…", that is, the punishment of their mockery.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {كَيفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَة}: عَاقِبَة is the noun (ism) of كَانَ, and كَيفَ is the predicate (khabar) of كَانَ. He did not say كَانَت because عاقبتهم ("their end") means مصيرهم ("their outcome"), and because the femininity of العاقبة is not real (ghayr ḥaqīqī).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {ليجمعنكم}: it is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from الرَّحْمَة, and the lām is the lām of the oath, so it is the answer to كتب, because كتب means "He made that obligatory upon Himself", so it carries the meaning of an oath.
His saying {الَّذين خسروا أنفسهم}: الَّذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and فهم لَا يُؤمنُونَ, a mubtadaʾ and khabar, stands in the position of the khabar of الَّذين. Al-Akhfash permitted الَّذين to be in the position of the accusative as a badal from the kāf and mīm in ليجمعنكم, but this is far-fetched, because a non-addressee is not substituted for an addressee: you do not say رَأَيْتُك زيدا ("I saw you, Zayd") as a badal.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {من يصرف عَنهُ}: whoever reads يصرف with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and a kasra on the rāʾ (يَصْرِف) makes the agent of يصرف latent, namely Allah, exalted be His mention, and implies an omitted object, its implied form being "whoever Allah turns the punishment away from on that Day". Whoever reads it with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on the rāʾ (يُصْرَف) implies only a deputy agent (lit. "an object whose agent is not named") and nothing else, its implied form being "whoever the punishment is turned away from on that Day". This involves less implication than the first, and according to Sībawayh, the less the implication, the better.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {شَهَادَة}: accusative as a clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).
His saying {وَمن بلغ}: مَن is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the kāf and mīm in لأنذركم, that is: "and that I may warn whomever the Qur'an reaches". It has also been said: whoever reaches puberty.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying {الَّذين آتَيْنَاهُم}: الَّذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is يعرفونه.
His saying {الَّذين خسروا}: nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, that is: "they are those who have lost".

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {وَمن أظلم}: مَن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is an interrogative in the sense of reproach, containing the meaning of negation, its implied form being "no one is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah". أظلم is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, except that it needs a completion, because مِمَّن افترى على الله كذبا is the completion of أظلم. Likewise with أفعل من كَذَا ("more … than such-and-such") wherever it occurs: مِن and what follows it are part of the completion of أفعل.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {ثمَّ لم تكن فتنتهم إِلَّا أَن قَالُوا}: whoever reads تكن with tāʾ makes it feminine because of the feminine form of الْفِتْنَة, makes الْفِتْنَة the noun (ism) of كَانَ and أَن قَالُوا the predicate (khabar) of كَانَ. Whoever reads يكن with yāʾ and puts the "fatḥa" [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently الفتنة "the fitna" is meant] in the accusative makes it the khabar of كَانَ and أَن قَالُوا the ism of كَانَ. Whoever reads تكن with tāʾ and puts الْفِتْنَة in the accusative makes it the khabar of كَانَ and makes تكن feminine according to the meaning, because أَن and what follows it is the fitna in meaning, since the ism of كَانَ is the khabar in meaning, as it enters upon a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Making أَن the ism of كَانَ is the preferred choice among the people of reasoning (ahl al-naẓar), because it can only be definite, since it cannot be qualified; it thus resembles the pronoun, and the pronoun is the most definite of definite nouns. So it is more fitting that the more definite be the ism of كَانَ than what is below it in definiteness, since الْفِتْنَة became definite only by its annexation to the pronoun, so it is far below أَن in definiteness. Whoever reads يكن with yāʾ and puts الْفِتْنَة in the nominative made it masculine because the femininity of الْفِتْنَة is not real, and because by الْفِتْنَة is meant "the excuse" (المعذرة), and المعذرة and العذر are the same; so he construed it according to the meaning and made it masculine, because the fitna is "the saying" in meaning, so he made it masculine, construing it according to the meaning.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying {أساطير}: its singular is أسطورة; it has also been said إسطارة; and it has also been said that it is the plural of a plural, its singular being أسطار, and أسطار is the plural of سطر. And أكنة is the plural of كنان.
His saying {من يستمع إِلَيْك}: مَن is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what precedes it is its khabar (predicate), namely وَمِنْهُم. He made يستمع singular because He construed it according to the form of مَن; had He made it plural in the speech according to the meaning, it would have been good, as He said in [Surat] Yūnus: وَمِنْهُم من يَسْتَمِعُون إِلَيْك.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying {وَلَا نكذب بآيَات رَبنَا ونكون}: whoever puts both verbs in the nominative (marfūʿ) conjoins them to نرد and makes all of it part of what the disbelievers wish for on the Day of Resurrection. They wished for three things: that they be returned; they wished that they had not belied the signs of Allah in the world; and they wished that they were among the believers. It is also possible that نكذب and نكون be in the nominative by way of disjunction (qaṭʿ), so that they do not enter into the wish, its implied form being: "Would that we were returned, and we will not belie and we will be among the believers, whether we are returned or not"; just as Sībawayh reported دَعْنِي وَلَا أَعُود ("Leave me, and I will not do it again"), that is: "and I will not do it again, whether you leave me or not"; he was not asking that leaving and not returning be combined for him. What supports the nominative by way of disjunction, in the meaning we mentioned, is His saying وَإِنَّهُم لَكَاذِبُونَ ("and indeed they are liars"): their being called liars shows that they were only reporting about themselves with that and were not wishing for it, because a wish is not answered by calling it a lie; calling something a lie only applies to a report (khabar). Some of the people of reasoning said: lying cannot occur in the Hereafter; it can only occur in this world. He interpreted His saying, Exalted is He, وانهم لَكَاذِبُونَ as "they are liars in this world in their belying the messengers and their denial of the resurrection", so that it is a narration of the state they were in in this world. Abū ʿAmr and others permitted that they be called liars in the Hereafter, because they claimed that if they were returned they would not belie the signs of Allah and that they would believe; but Allah knew what would not be, if it were to be, how it would be, and that if they were returned they would not believe and would belie the signs of Allah; so Allah declared them liars in their claim. As for whoever puts both verbs in the accusative, that is as the answer to the wish, because a wish is not an affirmed statement (ghayr wājib); so the two verbs enter into the wish, like the first of the two aspects of the nominative. The accusative is by an implied أَن, construed upon the maṣdar of نرد: أَن is implied so that together with the verb it forms a maṣdar, and a maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar with the wāw, its implied form being: "Would that we had a return, and a refraining from belying, and a being among the believers". As for whoever puts نكذب in the nominative and نكون in the accusative, he put نكذب in the nominative according to one of the first two aspects: either it enters into the wish, so it has the meaning of the accusative, or it is nominative as a firm, affirmative statement, as has preceded, that is: "and we will not belie, whether we are returned or not"; and he put نكون in the accusative as the answer to the wish, as has preceded, so it enters into the wish.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying {بَغْتَة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and according to Sībawayh analogy is not made on it: if you said جَاءَ زيد سرعَة ("Zayd came quickness"), meaning مسرعا ("hurrying"), it would not be permissible.
His saying {سَاءَ مَا يزرون}: مَا is indefinite, in the position of the accusative by سَاءَ, and in سَاءَ there is a nominative pronoun explained by what follows it, as with نعم and بئس. It has also been said that مَا is in the position of the nominative by سَاءَ.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {وللدار الْآخِرَة خير}: الدَّار is a mubtadaʾ (subject), الْآخِرَة is a naʿt (adjective) of الدَّار, and خير is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. Usage has been extended with الْآخِرَة so that it was made to stand in place of the qualified noun, though originally it is an adjective; Allah the Exalted said وللآخرة خير لَك من الأولى. As for whoever reads ولدار with a single lām and annexes it to الْآخِرَة, he does not make الْآخِرَة an adjective of الدَّار; rather الْآخِرَة is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being "and the abode of the last Hour (ولدار السَّاعَة الْآخِرَة)"; then السَّاعَة was omitted, the adjective was made to stand in place of the qualified noun, and الدَّار was annexed to it. الْآخِرَة and الدُّنْيَا are originally adjectives, but usage was extended with them, so they were used as nouns are used and were annexed to.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {يكذبُونَك}: whoever reads it with a shadda (يُكَذِّبُونَك) takes it in the sense of "they do not ascribe lying to you", just as one says فسّقت الرجل and خطّأته when you ascribe immorality or error to him. As for whoever reads it without shadda (يُكْذِبُونَك), he takes it in the sense of "they do not find you lying", just as one says أحمدت الرجل and أبخلته when you find him praiseworthy or miserly. It is also possible that the meaning of the light and the doubled forms is the same, just as one says قلّلت and أقللت, and كثّرت and أكثرت, with one meaning.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying {قل أَرَأَيْتكُم}: the kāf and mīm are for address, and have no grammatical position according to the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ said: its form is the form of an accusative but its meaning is the meaning of a nominative. This is impossible, because the tāʾ would then be the kāf in أَرَأَيْتكُم, and so a sign of the plural would have had to appear on the tāʾ; and there would have had to be two agents for one verb while both refer to one thing; and your saying أرأيتك زيدا مَا صنع would have to mean "Have you considered yourself, Zayd, what did he do?", because the kāf is the addressee. This speech is impossible in meaning and self-contradictory in i'rab and meaning, because you ask about the addressee himself at the start of the question, then turn the question to someone else at the end of the speech; you address at first and then bring an absent person at the end; and because رأيت would then have three objects. None of this is permissible. If you said أرأيتك عَالما بزيد ("Do you consider yourself knowing about Zayd?"), the kāf would be in the position of the accusative, because its implied form is "Do you consider yourself knowing about Zayd?"; this is correct speech, and رأيت has passed to two objects, no more.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t:
His saying {إِلَّا مبشرين ومنذرين}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الْمُرْسلين.
His saying {فَمن آمن}: مَن is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is فَلَا خوف عَلَيْهِم.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t:
His saying {بِالْغَدَاةِ}: the alif and lām entered upon غَدَاة only because it is indefinite. Most of the Arabs treat غدْوَة as definite and so do not give it tanwīn, while all of them treat غَدَاة as indefinite and give it tanwīn; and some of them treat غدْوَة as indefinite, and they are the minority.
His saying {من حسابهم من شَيْء}: the first [مِن] is partitive and the second is redundant (zāʾida), and شَيْء is in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of مَا. Similar to it is وَمَا من حِسَابك عَلَيْهِم من شَيْء.
His saying {فَتَطْرُدهُمْ}: accusative because it is the answer to the negation; and فتكون is the answer to the prohibition in His saying وَلَا تطرد الَّذين.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {لِيَقُولُوا أَهَؤُلَاءِ}: this is the lām of purpose (lām kay). It entered only in the sense that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, already knew what they would say before they said it; so it came to mean: they were tried only so that they would say [it], according to what was already in Allah's knowledge. So it is by way of denial (inkār) on their part. It has also been said: rather it is by way of enquiry (istikhbār): they said, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour?"

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {كتب ربكُم على نَفسه الرَّحْمَة} أَنه … فَأَنَّهُ: whoever reads أَن with a fatḥa in both places makes the first a badal (substitute) from الرَّحْمَة, the substitution of a thing for what is identical to it; so it is in the position of the accusative governed by كتب. For the second he implies a khabar (predicate) and puts it in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or by the adverbial phrase (ẓarf), its implied form being "then for him is that his Lord is forgiving to him", that is, "then for him is his Lord's forgiveness". It is also possible to imply a mubtadaʾ and make أَن its khabar, its implied form being "then his affair is that his Lord is forgiving to him", that is, "then his affair is his Lord's forgiveness". Similar to it in the implied form, the omission and the i'rab is {فَأن لَهُ نَار جَهَنَّم} in Surat al-Tawba. It has been said that أَن in His saying فَأَنَّهُ is a repetition, so that it is in the position of the accusative, referred back to the first, as though it were a badal from the first. But this is far-fetched, because if مَن is a relative (mawṣūla) in the sense of الَّذِي and you make فَأَنَّهُ a badal from the first أَن, the mubtadaʾ, which is مَن, remains without a khabar; and if مَن is conditional, the condition remains without an apodosis (jawāb). Moreover, the presence of the fāʾ prevents substitution, because nothing comes between the badal and what it substitutes for except parenthetical elements, and the fāʾ is not one of the parenthetical elements. If you make the fāʾ redundant, that is not permissible, because the condition would remain without an apodosis if you make the second أَن a badal from the first, and the mubtadaʾ would remain without a khabar if you make مَن a relative and أَن a badal from the first. As for the kasra in both (إِنَّه … فَإِنَّه), it is as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), or on the implication of قَالَ ("He said"). The kasra after the fāʾ is better, because in most speech one begins anew with what comes after the fāʾ, so the kasra after it is better.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {ولتستبين سَبِيل}: whoever reads it with tāʾ and puts السَّبِيل in the accusative makes the tāʾ a sign of address and of the future, and implies the name of the Prophet in the verb [as its agent]. Whoever reads it with tāʾ and puts السَّبِيل in the nominative makes the tāʾ a sign of the feminine and of the future; there is no pronoun in the verb, and السَّبِيل is nominative as the agent of its verb. Sībawayh reported استبان الشَّيْء ("the thing became clear") and استبنته أَنا ("I made it clear"). As for whoever reads it with yāʾ and puts السَّبِيل in the nominative, he made السَّبِيل masculine because it is treated as both masculine and feminine, and put it in the nominative as the agent of its verb. And whoever reads it with yāʾ and puts السَّبِيل in the accusative implies the name of the Prophet in the verb, and it is the fāʿil (agent), and puts السَّبِيل in the accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The lām in لتستبين is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "and so that the way of the criminals may become clear, We have detailed them".

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying {أَن أعبد}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being نهيت عَن أَن أعبد ("I have been forbidden from worshipping").

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {وكذبتم بِهِ}: the hāʾ refers back to الْبَيِّنَة ("the clear proof"), and it is made masculine because it has the sense of الْبَيَان ("the clarification").

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {لَو أَن عِنْدِي}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the agent of its verb, on the implication of a verb, and this has been mentioned before.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t: His saying {من ورقة}: مِن is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis and conveys generality, and ورقة is in the position of the nominative as the agent of تسقط; and likewise وَلَا حَبَّة. It is also permissible to put حَبَّة in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise {وَلَا رطب وَلَا يَابِس}. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read رطب and يابس in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar (predicate) being {إِلَّا فِي كتاب مُبين}.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His saying {مَوْلَاهُم الْحق}: مَوْلَاهُم is a badal (substitute) from the name of Allah, and الْحق is a naʿt (adjective) of مولاهم. Al-Ḥasan read الْحق in the accusative, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or on the implication of أَعنِي ("I mean").

mekki-muskil:63-63.t: His saying {تضرعا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "possessed of humility" (ذوي تضرع).

mekki-muskil:65-65.t: His saying {شيعًا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:69-69.t: His saying {وَلَكِن ذكرى}: ذكرى is in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with an omitted khabar (predicate), its implied form being "but upon them is a reminder" (وَلَكِن عَلَيْهِم ذكرى).

mekki-muskil:70-70.t: His saying {أَن تبسل}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: "lest it be given up to destruction" and "for fear that it be given up to destruction".

mekki-muskil:71-71.t: His saying {حيران}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), but it is a diptote because it is like غضبان.

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {وَأَن أقِيمُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being وَبِأَن أقِيمُوا ("and with: establish…"). It has also been said that it is conjoined to the meaning of لنسلم, because its implied form is لِأَن نسلم ("that we submit"). And it has been said that it is conjoined to the meaning of ائتنا, because its meaning is أَن ائتنا ("that: come to us").

mekki-muskil:73-73.t:
His saying {وَيَوْم يَقُول}: يَوْم is accusative by conjunction to the hāʾ in اتقوه, that is: "fear Him, and fear the day on which He says". It may also be conjoined to السَّمَوَات, that is: "He created the heavens and created the day on which He says". It has also been said that it is accusative on the implication of "and remember, O Muḥammad, the day on which He says".
His saying {كن فَيكون}: that is, "then it is" (فَهُوَ يكون); that is why it is in the nominative. In يكون is its noun (ism), and it is complete (tāmma, i.e. "to come into being"), not needing a predicate; and likewise كن. The latent pronoun is the pronoun of الصُّور ("the forms"), mention of which comes after it, with the intention of placing it before يكون. It has also been said that the implied form of the latent pronoun in فَيكون is "then all that He willed comes to be". It has also been said that قَوْله is the noun of فَيكون and الْحق is its adjective. And it has been said that قَوْله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الْحق is its khabar (predicate).
His saying {يَوْم ينْفخ فِي الصُّور}: يَوْم is a badal (substitute) from يَوْم يَقُول. It has also been said that what puts it in the accusative is لَهُ الْملك, that is: "His is the dominion on the day the trumpet is blown".
His saying {عَالم الْغَيْب}: a naʿt (adjective) of الَّذي, or nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is the Knower of the unseen". It may also be nominative construed according to the meaning, that is: "the Knower blows into it" — as though, when He said ينْفخ فِي الصُّور and it was asked "Who blows into it?", it was said "The Knower of the unseen blows into it"; as the poet said:
... ليبك يزِيد ضارع لخصومة ...
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let] one humbled in a dispute [weep for him].)
as though it were asked "Who should weep for him?", and it was said "One humbled". Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read عَالم الْغَيْب in the genitive, as a badal from the hāʾ in لَهُ.

mekki-muskil:74-74.t: His saying {لِأَبِيهِ آزر}: whoever reads آزر with a fatḥa places it in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from الْأَب, as though it were his name. Yaʿqūb and others read it in the nominative, as a vocative, as though he made آزر a nickname for him, its interpretation being: "O crooked in religion! Do you take idols as gods?"

mekki-muskil:75-75.t: His saying {وليكون من الموقنين}: the lām is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "and so that he would be among those of certainty, We showed him the dominion (الملكوت)".

mekki-muskil:80-80.t:
His saying {أتحاجوني}: whoever reads the nūn light only dropped the second [nūn], which came in with the yāʾ that is the first-person pronoun, because two identical letters came together along with frequency of use, and he left the nūn that is the sign of the nominative. There is some ugliness in this, because he gave it a kasra on account of its adjacency to the yāʾ, while its due is the fatḥa; so both omission and alteration occurred in the word. Whoever reads it with a shadda assimilated the first nūn into the second, and this has parallels. Whoever claims that it is the first that is dropped only takes as his evidence the kasra of the [remaining] second nūn; but this is not permissible, because the first nūn is the sign of the nominative, and the nominative is not dropped from verbs without a jussive-making or accusative-making particle. What shows that it is the second, not the first, that is dropped is that the heaviness only arises with the second; and what also shows it is their saying ليتي for لَيْتَني, dropping the nūn that goes with the yāʾ.
His saying {علما}: accusative as a specification (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).

mekki-muskil:82-82.t: His saying {الَّذين آمنُوا وَلم يلبسوا}: الَّذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); أُولَئِكَ is a badal (substitute) from الَّذين or a second mubtadaʾ; الْأَمْن is a third or second mubtadaʾ; لَهُم is the khabar (predicate) of الْأَمْن; الْأَمْن with its khabar is the khabar of أُولَئِكَ; أُولَئِكَ with its khabar is the khabar of الَّذين; and وهم مهتدون is a mubtadaʾ and khabar.

mekki-muskil:83-83.t: His saying {نرفع دَرَجَات من نشَاء}: whoever gives دَرَجَات tanwīn makes نرفع act upon مَن, and puts دَرَجَات in the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), or by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "to degrees" (إِلَى دَرَجَات), as He the Exalted said {وَرفع بَعضهم دَرَجَات}. Whoever does not give it tanwīn puts دَرَجَات in the accusative by نرفع as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and annexes it to مَن. Similar to it is the one in [Surat] Yūsuf.

mekki-muskil:84-84.t: His saying {كلا هدينَا}: كلا is accusative by هدينا, and likewise نوحًا هدينَا. وَدَاوُد and what follows it are conjoined to نوح. The hāʾ in ذُريَّته refers back to Nūḥ (Noah); it cannot refer back to Ibrāhīm (Abraham), because after it comes ولوطا, and Lūṭ (Lot) was only of the offspring of Nūḥ and lived in the time of Ibrāhīm, so he is not of the offspring of Ibrāhīm. It has been said that he was the son of Ibrāhīm's brother, and it has been said: the son of his sister.

mekki-muskil:86-86.t: His saying / اليسع /: it is a definite foreign (aʿjamī) name, and the alif and lām in it are redundant. It has also been said that it is an imperfect verb used as a name, then made indefinite, so the two letters of definiteness entered it. Whoever reads it with two lāms (اللَّيْسَع) also makes it a foreign name on the pattern فَيْعَل, made indefinite so that the two letters of definiteness entered it; its origin is ليسع. The origin in the other reading is يسع; so its origin, according to the view of whoever makes it an imperfect verb used as a name, is يُوسع; then the wāw was dropped as it was dropped in يعد. The fatḥa on the sīn did not have an effect [preventing the dropping], because it is an acquired fatḥa necessitated by the ʿayn [Translator's note: i.e. the guttural letter], and its origin is the kasra; so the dropping took place on the assumption of the original form.

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His saying {لَيْسُوا بهَا بكافرين}: the first bāʾ is attached to كافرين, and the second entered to emphasise the negation; and it [كافرين] is the khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ.

mekki-muskil:90-90.t: His saying {فبهداهم اقتده}: the hāʾ entered to make clear the vowel of the dāl, and it is the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt). As for whoever gives it a kasra, it is possible that he made it the pronoun hāʾ, implying the maṣdar (verbal noun). It has also been said that he likened the hāʾ of pausing to the pronoun hāʾ and so gave it a kasra; but this is far-fetched.

mekki-muskil:91-91.t:
His saying {من شَيْء}: شَيْء is in the position of the accusative governed by أنزل, and مِن is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis and generality.
His saying {نورا وَهدى}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الْكتاب or from the hāʾ in بِهِ. Likewise تجعلونه is a ḥāl from الْكتاب, and تبدونها is a naʿt (adjective) of القراطيس. The implied form is "you put it in pages (فِي قَرَاطِيس)"; when the preposition was dropped, it became accusative.
His saying {وتخفون}: a new beginning (mubtadaʾ [clause]) with no grammatical position.
His saying يَلْعَبُونَ: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in ذرهم.

mekki-muskil:92-92.t:
His saying {مُصدق الَّذِي}: a naʿt (adjective) of الْكتاب, on the assumption that the tanwīn has been dropped from مُصدق because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and الَّذِي is in the position of the accusative governed by مُصدق. If you do not assume the dropping of the tanwīn, مُصدق الَّذِي is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, and الَّذِي is in the position of the genitive.
His saying {ولتنذر أم الْقرى}: the lām is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "and so that you may warn the Mother of Cities, We sent it down".

mekki-muskil:93-93.t:
His saying {وَمن قَالَ سَأُنْزِلُ}: مَن is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to مَن in His saying مِمَّن افترى.
His saying {وَالْمَلَائِكَة باسطوا أَيْديهم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الظَّالِمين. The hāʾ and mīm in أَيْديهم are for the angels. The implied form is: "while the angels are stretching out their hands with punishment against the wrongdoers, saying to them: 'Bring out your souls'"; so the "saying" is implied. What indicates this meaning is His saying in another place يضْربُونَ وُجُوههم وأدبارهم ("striking their faces and their backs"). The meaning of His saying اخْرُجُوا أَنفسكُم is: "rescue yourselves today from what has befallen you"; so what puts اليوم in the accusative is اخْرُجُوا, and on this view pausing on it is good. It has also been said that what puts it in the accusative is تُجْزونَ, so one does not pause on it but begins with it. The apodosis (jawāb) of لَو is omitted, its implied form being: "If you could see, O Muḥammad, when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, you would see a tremendous thing".

mekki-muskil:94-94.t:
His saying {فُرَادَى}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent nominative pronoun in جئتمونا. It is a diptote because it contains the alif of the feminine. Abū Ḥaywa read it with tanwīn, and that is a dialect of some of Tamīm. The kāf in كَمَا is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "And you have come to Us alone, a being-alone like your state the first time".
His saying {لقد تقطع بَيْنكُم}: whoever puts بَيْنكُم in the nominative makes it the fāʿil (agent) of تقطع, and makes البين mean "union" (الوصل), its implied form being "your union has been severed", that is: "[your] uniting has broken apart; between [means] separation" [Translator's note: the text here reads أي تفرق واصل بين الافتراق, which appears corrupt; the sense intended is that بين originally denotes separation], but usage was extended with it, and it was used as a noun, not an adverb, in the sense of union. As for whoever puts it in the accusative, that is as an adverbial (ẓarf), and what governs it is what the speech indicates, namely the absence of their union; so its implied form is "your union between you has been severed", and the implied "your union" is what puts بين in the accusative. It has also been said that whoever puts بَيْنكُم in the accusative makes it nominative in meaning as the agent of تقطع, but since it occurs in most speech in the accusative, he left it in its state when it is in the nominative position; this is the view of al-Akhfash. So according to this, the two readings have one meaning. Of this kind, according to al-Akhfash, is His saying وَمنا دون ذَلِك, and similar to it is يفصل بَيْنكُم in the reading of those who put a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on the ṣād (يُفْصَلُ). So دون and بين are used in these places as nouns, not adverbs, but they were left with the fatḥa while their position is nominative, because they are mostly used in the accusative as adverbs.

mekki-muskil:96-96.t:
His saying {وَالشَّمْس وَالْقَمَر}: they are accusative by conjunction to the position of اللَّيْل, because it is in the position of the accusative. It has also been said: rather, on the implication of وَجعل ("and He made"). As for whoever reads وَجعل اللَّيْل, it is conjunction on the form and the meaning.
His saying {حسبانا}: al-Akhfash said: its meaning is "by reckoning" (بحسبان); when the preposition was dropped, it became accusative. It has also been said that حسبانا is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حسبت الشَّيْء حسبانا وحسبا ("I reckoned the thing"), and الحساب is the noun.

mekki-muskil:98-98.t: His saying {فمستقر ومستودع}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, that is: "then of you is one settled and of you is one deposited". Whoever reads the qāf with a fatḥa (مُسْتَقَر), its implied form is "then for you is a place of settlement", that is, a place of settlement in the wombs and a place of deposit in the earth. It has also been said that the place of deposit is what was in the loins. And it has been said that مستقر means "in the grave", on the reading of whoever reads the qāf with a kasra (مُسْتَقِر).

mekki-muskil:99-99.t:
His saying {وجنات من أعناب}: whoever reads جنَّات in the accusative conjoins it to نَبَات. The nominative has been transmitted from ʿĀṣim, in the sense of "and they have gardens", as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It is not permissible to conjoin it to قنوان, because the gardens do not come from the date palms.
His saying {انْظُرُوا إِلَى ثمره}: whoever reads it with two fatḥas (ثَمَره) makes it the plural of ثَمَرَة, like بقرة and بقر, and the plural of the plural is ثمار, like أكمة and آكام. Whoever reads it with two ḍammas (ثُمُره) also makes it the plural of ثَمَرَة, like خشبة and خشب. It has also been said that it is the plural of a plural, as though it were the plural of ثمار, like حمار and حمر; so ثُمُر is the plural of ثمار, and ثمار is the plural of ثَمَرَة.

mekki-muskil:100-100.t: His saying {وَجعلُوا لله شُرَكَاء الْجِنّ}: الْجِنّ is the first object of جعل, and شُرَكَاء is the second object, placed first; the lām in لله is attached to شُرَكَاء. If you wish, you may make شُرَكَاء the first object and الْجِنّ a badal (substitute) from شُرَكَاء, with لله in the position of the second object, the lām being attached to جعل. Al-Kisāʾī permitted الْجِنّ in the nominative, in the sense of "they are the jinn".

mekki-muskil:105-105.t:
His saying {وَكَذَلِكَ نصرف}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "and We vary the signs with a varying like what We have recited to you".
His saying {وليقولوا درست}: the lām is attached to something omitted, its implied form being: "and so that they may say 'you have studied', We varied the signs"; and similar to it is ولنبينه. The meaning of درست, in the reading of whoever puts a fatḥa on the tāʾ (دَرَسْتَ), is "you learned and read". Whoever makes it vowelless (دَرَسَتْ), its meaning is "they have become obsolete and effaced". And whoever reads it with an alif (دارست), its meaning is "you studied with the People of the Book and they studied with you".

mekki-muskil:108-108.t: His saying {عدوا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:109-109.t: His saying {مَا يشعركم أَنَّهَا إِذا جَاءَت}: whoever reads أَن with a fatḥa makes it mean لَعَلَّ ("perhaps"). Al-Khalīl reported from the Arabs: ائْتِ السُّوق أَنَّك تشتري لنا شَيْئا ("Go to the market; perhaps you will buy something for us"), that is, لَعَلَّك. مَا is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and in يشعركم there is an agent pronoun referring back to مَا. The meaning is: "And what makes you know of their faith when the sign comes to them? Perhaps when it comes to them they will not believe." So there is an omission in the speech indicated by what follows it, and the omitted element is the second object of يشعركم; one says شَعرت بالشَّيْء ("I perceived the thing"), that is, I came to know it. Had أَن been taken in its normal function, that would have been an excuse for them; but it is in the sense of لَعَلَّ. It has also been said that أَن is accusative by يشعركم, but that لَا is redundant (zāʾida) in His saying لَا يُؤمنُونَ, the implied form being: "And what makes you know that the sign, when it comes to them, they will believe?" It is an address to the believers, meaning that those of the disbelievers who demanded the sign would not believe if it came to them. So أَن is the second object of يشعركم according to this view, and there is no omission in the speech.

mekki-muskil:110-110.t: His saying {أول مرّة}: accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), meaning: in this world.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t:
His saying {قبلا}: whoever reads it with a kasra on the qāf and a fatḥa on the bāʾ (قِبَلا) puts it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, and it has the sense of "face to face" or "openly", that is, they would be facing it. Likewise whoever reads it with a ḍamma on the qāf and the bāʾ (قُبُلا): it is also accusative as a ḥāl, in the sense of "guarantors", or in the sense of "group by group" (قبيلا قبيلا).
His saying {إِلَّا أَن يَشَاء الله}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

mekki-muskil:112-112.t:
His saying {شياطين الْإِنْس وَالْجِنّ}: accusative as a badal (substitute) from عَدو, or as the second object of جعل.
His saying {غرُورًا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:114-114.t:
His saying {حكما}: accusative as a clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and أبتغي is made transitive to غير.
His saying {منزل من رَبك بِالْحَقِّ}: بِالْحَقِّ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in منزل. It cannot be an object of منزل, because منزل has already passed to two objects: one of them by means of a preposition, namely من رَبك, and the second latent in منزل, which is the one standing in place of the agent; it is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil; lit. "an object whose agent is not named"), referring back to الْكتاب.

mekki-muskil:115-115.t: His saying {صدقا وعدلا}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns); if you wish, you may place them in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "truthful" and "just".

mekki-muskil:117-117.t: His saying {هُوَ أعلم من يضل}: مَن is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is interrogative, and يضل عَن سَبيله is the khabar (predicate). It has also been said that مَن is in the position of the accusative by a verb indicated by أعلم, and it has the sense of الَّذِي, its implied form being: "and He is most knowing; He knows who goes astray". It is unlikely that مَن is accusative by أعلم, because of its remoteness from resembling the verb, and abstract governors (al-maʿānī) do not govern objects as they govern adverbials. Nor is it good to take it as a verb of the speaker reporting about himself [i.e. أُعْلِمُ, "I make known"], because it is in the form of reporting about an absent one. Nor is it good to take it in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil, "knowing"), since it is not good to take it as a verb; أفعل has the sense of fāʿil only when it is good to take it as a verb of the speaker reporting about himself. Nor is it good to assume the omission of a preposition, because that belongs to the necessities of poetry. Nor is annexation good in it, because that would be disbelief, since أفعل is annexed only to that of which it is a part — so understand it — unless it is in the sense of fāʿil, in which case it is good to annex it to that of which it is not a part, as in وَأعلم مَا تبدون, because tanwīn and separation are implied in it.

mekki-muskil:119-119.t:
His saying {وَمَا لكم أَلا تَأْكُلُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition. مَا is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is its khabar (predicate), its implied form being: "And what is there for you in not eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned?"
His saying {إِلَّا مَا اضطررتم}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā).

mekki-muskil:122-122.t:
His saying {أَو من كَانَ مَيتا}: مَن has the sense of الَّذِي and is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the kāf in كمن is its khabar (predicate). In كَانَ is its noun (ism), referring back to مَن, and مَيتا is the predicate of كَانَ.
His saying {كمن مثله فِي الظُّلُمَات}: مثله is a mubtadaʾ and فِي الظُّلُمَات is its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of مَن; its implied form is "like one who is in the darkness".
His saying {لَيْسَ بِخَارِج مِنْهَا}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent nominative pronoun in His saying فِي الظُّلُمَات. The kāf in His saying كَذَلِك زين is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "it was made fair-seeming, a making fair-seeming like that; to the disbelievers their deeds were made fair-seeming".

mekki-muskil:123-123.t:
His saying {جعلنَا فِي كل قَرْيَة أكَابِر مجرميها}: مجرميها is in the position of the accusative by جعلنا as the first object, and أكَابِر is made the second object; in our view this is the correct meaning, as He said أمرنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا, that is, "We made them numerous", and as He said وأترفناهم فِي الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا, that is, "We gave them ease".
His saying {ليمكروا فِيهَا}: the lām is the lām of purpose (lām kay). Its meaning is that since Allah knew they would plot, the meaning became that it was made fair-seeming to them only so that they would plot, since their doing that had already preceded in His knowledge.

mekki-muskil:125-125.t:
His saying {ضيقا}: the second object of جعل, and حرجا is a naʿt (adjective) of it. If you wish, you may also make it an object by way of repetition: just as a second predicate or more may come for a single mubtadaʾ, so two objects or more may stand in the position of one object. This happens only with what enters upon a mubtadaʾ and khabar. You say طَعَامك حُلْو حامض مر ("your food is sweet, sour, bitter"): these are three predicates about the food, meaning that your food combines these tastes. If you bring in upon the mubtadaʾ a verb that puts two objects in the accusative, such as ظَنَنْت, or كَانَ, or إِن, all the predicates become accusative — or nominative as predicates of إِن. You say ظَنَنْت طَعَامك حلوا حامضا مرا, and likewise with كَانَ. So what is permissible with the mubtadaʾ is permissible with what enters upon the mubtadaʾ. Likewise جعل enters upon a mubtadaʾ: it is as though, before it entered, it was صَدره ضيق حرج ("his breast is narrow, constricted"), so ضيق and حرج are a predicate after a predicate; when جعل entered, it put the mubtadaʾ and its two predicates in the accusative. This is on the reading of whoever reads it with a kasra on the rāʾ (حَرِجا), because he makes it an active participle, like دنف and فرق; and the meaning of حرج is like the meaning of ضيق, repeated for emphasis because its wording differs. As for whoever reads the rāʾ with a fatḥa (حَرَجا), it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said that it is the plural of حرجة, like قصبة and قصب.
His saying {كَأَنَّمَا يصعد}: the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in حرج or in ضيق.
His saying {كَذَلِك يَجْعَل الله}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "a making like that, Allah makes".

mekki-muskil:126-126.t:
His saying {مُسْتَقِيمًا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from صِرَاط. This is called the corroborative ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muʾakkida), because the path of Allah can only be straight; so it was not brought to distinguish between two states, since the path of Allah never changes from straightness. This ḥāl is not like the ḥāl in your saying هَذَا زيد رَاكِبًا ("this is Zayd, riding"), because Zayd may at another time be free of riding, passing to its opposite, whereas the path of Allah is never free of straightness. So recognise the meaning of the corroborative ḥāl as distinct from the ḥāl that distinguishes between actions that differ and change.
His saying {وَيَوْم نحشرهم جَمِيعًا}: يَوْم is accusative by an implied verb, its meaning being "and remember, O Muḥammad, the day We gather them". It has also been said that it is accusative by an implied يقول ("He will say"). And His saying جَمِيعًا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in نحشرهم.

mekki-muskil:128-128.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ الله}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). If you take مَا as referring to rational beings, it is not disconnected.

mekki-muskil:130-130.t: His saying {يقصون}: in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رسل; and likewise وينذرونكم.

mekki-muskil:131-131.t: His saying {ذَلِك أَن لم يكن}: ذَلِك is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is that". Al-Farrāʾ permitted ذَلِك to be in the position of the accusative on the implication of "Allah did that". And أَن is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being لِأَن لم يكن ("because … was not"); when the preposition was dropped, it became accusative.

mekki-muskil:133-133.t: His saying {كَمَا أنشأكم}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a making-successors like His producing you".

mekki-muskil:134-134.t: His saying {إِن مَا توعدون لآت}: مَا has the sense of الَّذِي and is the noun (ism) of إِن. The hāʾ is omitted with توعدون, its implied form being توعدونه; it was omitted because of the length of the noun [with its ṣila]. لآت is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and the lām is the lām of emphasis.

mekki-muskil:135-135.t: His saying {من تكون لَهُ}: if you take مَن as interrogative, it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative by تعلمون. And if you take it in the sense of الَّذِي [with what follows as its ṣila] [Translator's note: the text here has خبرا, which appears to be an intrusion], it is in the position of the accusative by تعلمون.

mekki-muskil:136-136.t: His saying {سَاءَ مَا يحكمون}: مَا is in the position of the nominative by سَاءَ.

mekki-muskil:137-137.t: His saying {وَكَذَلِكَ زين لكثير}, the verse: whoever reads زين with a ḍamma, as a passive (lit. "of that whose agent is not named"), puts قتل in the nominative as the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil), annexes it to الْأَوْلَاد, and puts الشُّرَكَاء in the nominative, construed according to the meaning, as though it were asked "Who made it fair-seeming to them?" and the answer were "their partners". The partners are annexed to them because it was they who contrived them (استخرقوها) [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps for اخترعوها "invented them"] and made them partners to Allah — Allah is exalted above that; so because of their contriving them, they were annexed to them. Whoever reads with this reading but puts الْأَوْلَاد in the accusative and الشُّرَكَاء in the genitive — that is a far-fetched reading, and it has been transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir; its justification is the separation of the muḍāf from the muḍāf ilayhi by the object, and that is only permissible, according to the grammarians, in poetry, and it mostly occurs with adverbials. It is also transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir that he read زين with a ḍamma on the zāy, قتل in the nominative, and الْأَوْلَاد and الشُّرَكَاء in the genitive. This too is far-fetched, and its justification is to make الشُّرَكَاء a badal (substitute) from الْأَوْلَاد, so that الشُّرَكَاء becomes a name for the children because they share with the fathers in lineage, inheritance and religion.

mekki-muskil:138-138.t:
His saying {إِلَّا من نشَاء}: مَن is in the position of the nominative as the agent of يطعم.
His saying {افتراء}: a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:139-139.t:
His saying {مَا فِي بطُون}: مَا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is خَالِصَة. The predicate was made feminine only because what is in the bellies of the cattle is cattle, so the femininity was construed according to the meaning. Then He said ومحرم, making it masculine, construing it according to the form of مَا. This is rare and without parallel: with مَن and مَا the speech is normally construed first according to the form and then according to the meaning after that, whereas here the wording came first construed according to the meaning and was then construed according to the form after that; so take note of it, for it is uncommon. It has also been said that it was made feminine for intensiveness, like راوية and علامة. Qatāda read خَالِصَة in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent nominative pronoun in His saying فِي بطُون, with the khabar of مَا being لذكورنا. It is not permissible for the ḥāl to be from the latent nominative pronoun in لذكورنا, because the ḥāl does not precede its governor, according to Sībawayh and others, when [the governor] is not fully inflectable [Translator's note: i.e. not a verb]: if you said زيد قَائِما فِي الدَّار it would not be permissible, though al-Akhfash permitted it. Ibn ʿAbbās read خَالِص in the masculine [Translator's note: the text reads خَالِصَة بالتذكير, "خالصة in the masculine"; evidently خالصُه is meant], referring back to the form of مَا, and put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with لذكورنا as the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of مَا. It is also possible that خَالِصَة is a badal (substitute) from مَا, the substitution of a thing for a thing that is part of it, with لذكورنا as the khabar. Al-Aʿmash read خَالص without hāʾ, referring it back to the form of مَا, and put it in the nominative: it is a second mubtadaʾ, لذكورنا is the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of مَا.
His saying {وَإِن يكن ميتَة}: whoever puts ميتَة in the accusative and reads with yāʾ referred it back to the form of مَا and implied the noun of يكن in it, with ميتَة as its predicate, its implied form being "and if what is in their bellies is carrion". Whoever reads تكن with tāʾ made it feminine according to the femininity of the cattle that are in the bellies, its implied form being "and if the cattle that are in their bellies are carrion". Whoever puts ميتَة in the nominative makes كَانَ mean "occur" and "happen", complete (tāmma), not needing a predicate. Al-Akhfash said: the predicate is implied, its implied form according to him being "and if there is carrion in their bellies".

mekki-muskil:140-140.t: His saying {سفها}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); if you wish, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:141-141.t: His saying {وَالنَّخْل وَالزَّرْع}: conjoined to جنَّات, and مختلفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being, that is, "it will be (سيكون) so" [Translator's note: the text reads أي سكون كذلك, evidently for أي سيكون كذلك], because at the beginning of their coming out of the earth there is no produce in them that could be described as differing in taste; rather, that difference is found in them when they bear fruit. So it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), that is, the matter will be so. When you say رَأَيْت زيدا قَائِما ("I saw Zayd standing"), you are only reporting that you saw him in this state, so it is an actual ḥāl, not awaited. But when you say خلق الله النّخل مُخْتَلفا أكله ("Allah created the date palms differing in their produce"), you are not reporting that He created them while there was in them produce of differing colour and taste; that is only something awaited to be in them when they bear fruit, so it is an awaited, anticipated ḥāl. Likewise, when you say رَأَيْت زيدا مُسَافِرًا غَدا ("I saw Zayd travelling tomorrow"), you did not see him in the state of travel; it is only something you anticipate will be tomorrow. So recognise the difference between the actual ḥāl, the anticipated awaited ḥāl, and the corroborative ḥāl which we mentioned in His saying صِرَاط رَبك مُسْتَقِيمًا. These are three ḥāls with different meanings, so understand them and recognise them, for there is much of this in the Qur'an. Of it is His saying لتدخلن الْمَسْجِد الْحَرَام إِن شَاءَ الله آمِنين: آمِنين is an anticipated, awaited ḥāl; and there is much like it.

mekki-muskil:142-142.t: His saying {وَمن الْأَنْعَام حمولة وفرشا}: accusative by conjunction to جنَّات, that is: "and He produced of the cattle حمولة" — the large ones, made docile and capable of carrying heavy loads — "and فرشا" — the small ones.

mekki-muskil:143-143.t:
His saying {ثَمَانِيَة أَزوَاج}: al-Kisāʾī said: ثَمَانِيَة is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "He produced eight". Al-Akhfash said: it is a badal (substitute) from حمولة and فرش. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "eat the meat of eight pairs"; so the verb and the muḍāf were dropped, and the muḍāf ilayhi, which is ثَمَانِيَة, was made to stand in place of the muḍāf, which is لحم. It has also been said that it is accusative as a badal from مَا in His saying كلوا مِمَّا رزقكم الله, according to its position.
His saying {آلذكرين حرم}: accusative by حرم; وَأم الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ is conjoined to الذكرين, and مَا is also conjoined to it in His saying أم مَا اشْتَمَلت عَلَيْهِ. Abū Jaʿfar read على طاعم يطعمهُ with a shadda on the ṭāʾ and a kasra on the ʿayn (يَطَّعِمُه), as well as reading it light; its origin is يطتعمه on the pattern يفتعله, then the tāʾ was replaced by ṭāʾ and the first ṭāʾ was assimilated into it.

mekki-muskil:145-145.t:
His saying {إِلَّا أَن يكون ميتَة}: whoever reads it with yāʾ and puts ميتَة in the accusative implies a masculine [noun] in كَانَ as its noun (ism), its implied form being "unless what is eaten is carrion" or "unless that is carrion". Whoever reads it with tāʾ and puts ميتَة in the accusative implies "the eaten [thing]" in the feminine. Abū Jaʿfar read إِلَّا أَن تكون with tāʾ and ميتَة in the nominative, making كَانَ mean "occur" and "happen", and أَن is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It would have been incumbent on Abū Jaʿfar to read أَو دم in the nominative, and likewise what follows it; but he conjoined it to أَن and did not conjoin it to ميتَة. Whoever puts ميتَة in the accusative conjoins أَو دَمًا and what follows it to it.
His saying {أَو فسقا}: conjoined to لحم خِنْزِير and what precedes it.
His saying {فَإِنَّهُ رِجْس}: a parenthesis between the maʿṭūf (conjoined) and what it is conjoined to; it is intended to come after أَو فسقا.
His saying {غير بَاغ}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in اضطر.

mekki-muskil:146-146.t:
His saying {أَو الحوايا أَو مَا}: in the position of the nominative, conjoined to ظهورهما; and مَا in His saying إِلَّا مَا حملت is in the position of the accusative as an exception from الشحوم.
His saying {الحوايا}: its singular is حوية; it has also been said حاوية; and it has also been said حاوياء, like نافقاء. الحوايا is in the position of the nominative according to al-Kisāʾī, by conjunction to الظُّهُور, in the sense of "except what the entrails carry". Others said: it is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to مَا in His saying إِلَّا مَا حملت.
His saying {ذَلِك جزيناهم ببغيهم}: ذَلِك is in the position of the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "the matter is that". It may also be in the position of the accusative by جزيناهم.

mekki-muskil:147-147.t: His saying {ذُو رَحْمَة}: the origin of ذُو is ذوى, like عصى; that is why He said in the dual ذواتا أفنان.

mekki-muskil:150-150.t: His saying {هَلُمَّ}: its origin is هَا المم; the vowel of the first mīm was transferred to the lām and [the mīm] was assimilated into the second. When the lām took a vowel, the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was no longer needed, and two vowelless letters met: the alif of هَا and the lām of المم, since its vowel is incidental. So its alif was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the hāʾ joined to the lām, which bears a ḍamma, followed by a doubled mīm, so it became هَلُمَّ as it is in the recitation. When it changed, its meaning changed, and it was used in the sense of تعال ("come") and in the sense of ائْتِ ("bring").

mekki-muskil:151-151.t:
His saying {أَلا تُشْرِكُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from مَا in His saying أتل مَا. It may also be in the position of the nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is that you do not associate".
His saying {ذَلِكُم وَصَّاكُم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:153-153.t: His saying {وَأَن هَذَا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition, that is, "and because this…" (وَلِأَن هَذَا). Whoever reads it with a kasra makes it begin a new sentence. Whoever reads it with a fatḥa and light makes it the lightened form of the heavy [أَنَّ], in the position of the accusative like the first. And مستقيما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from صِرَاطِي, and it is the corroborative ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muʾakkida).

mekki-muskil:154-154.t:
His saying {تَمامًا}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying {على الَّذِي أحسن}: whoever puts أحسن in the nominative implies هُوَ as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with أحسن as its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذِي. Whoever reads it with a fatḥa makes it a past verb, the ṣila of الَّذِي, with a pronoun in it referring back to الَّذِي, its implied form being "a completion for the one who did good". It has also been said that there is no pronoun in أحسن, the agent is omitted and the hāʾ is omitted, its implied form being "a completion of that which Allah bestowed well upon Mūsā (Moses) of the message".

mekki-muskil:156-156.t:
His saying {أَن تَقولُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying {وَإِن كُنَّا عَن دراستهم لغافلين}: إن is lightened from the heavy [إنّ] according to the Basrans, and its noun is implied with it, its implied form being "and indeed we were". The Kufans said: إِن is in the sense of مَا, [and اللام] in the sense of إِلَّا, its implied form being "and we were nothing but heedless of their study" [Translator's note: the text says "إن in the sense of إلا", which compresses the Kufan view that إن is negative and the lām means إلا].
Ibn Sīrīn read لَا تَنْفَع with tāʾ, on the basis that the maṣdar may be treated as feminine or masculine, because الْإِيمَان, which is the agent of تَنْفَع, is a maṣdar. It has also been said that الْإِيمَان was made feminine only because it is included in النَّفس ("the soul").

mekki-muskil:160-160.t: His saying {فَلهُ عشر أَمْثَالهَا}: whoever annexes it (عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا), its meaning is "then for him are ten good deeds, the likes of a good deed". Whoever gives عشر tanwīn — and it is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash — its implied form is "then for him are good deeds, ten, the likes of it". All of it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is لَهُ. Allah increases in the multiplying whatever He wills for whomever He wills; ten is the minimum of the reward, and the bounty beyond that is for whomever Allah wills.

mekki-muskil:161-161.t:
His saying {دينا قيمًا}: دينا is accusative by an implied هداني, indicated by the first هَدَانِي. It has also been said that its implied form is "He made known to me a religion". And it has been said that it is a badal (substitute) from صِرَاط according to the position, because هَدَانِي إِلَى صِرَاط and هداني صراطا have one meaning; so it was construed according to the meaning and دينا was substituted for صِرَاط. Whoever reads قيمًا with a shadda (قَيِّمًا), its origin is قيوم on the pattern فَيْعِل; then the wāw was replaced by yāʾ and the yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ. Whoever reads it light (قِيَمًا) built it on the pattern فِعَل; its original form ought to have come with the wāw, so that one would say قِوَما, just as they said عوض and حول; but it deviated from the analogical rule.
His saying {مِلَّة إِبْرَاهِيم}: a badal (substitute) from دين.
His saying {حَنِيفا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِبْرَاهِيم; it has also been said that it is accusative on the implication of أَعنِي ("I mean").

mekki-muskil:162-162.t: His saying {ومحياي}: the due of the yāʾ is to have a fatḥa, as the kāf has in رَأَيْتُك and the tāʾ in قُمْت; but a vowel on the yāʾ is heavy. Whoever makes it vowelless does so for lightness, but he combines two vowelless letters; combining two vowelless letters is permissible when the first is a letter of prolongation and softness, because the prolongation in it stands in place of a vowel on which one rests, so it separates the two vowelless letters.

mekki-muskil:164-164.t: His saying {أغير الله}: accusative by أبغي, and ربا is accusative as a specification (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).

mekki-muskil:165-165.t: His saying {دَرَجَات}: that is, "to degrees" (إِلَى دَرَجَات); when the preposition was dropped, it became accusative.
